exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Strong Version C evidence combines an equation lock with an inequality lock to create and justify a two-digit master code.

traits.sample: Lock 1 is 6x = 42, so x = 7; substituting gives 6(7) = 42.
traits.why: The substitution check proves 7 makes the equation true.

traits.sample: Lock 2 is k > 7. I drew an open circle at 7 and shaded right; it has infinitely many solutions.
traits.why: The symbol, boundary point, shading, and solution set describe the same constraint.

traits.sample: I used the least whole-number solution to k > 7, which is 8. Equation digit 7 followed by inequality digit 8 makes code 78.
traits.why: The extra selection rule turns an infinite solution set into one unambiguous code digit.

traits.sample: Three of five trial teams solved both locks, so my observed solve rate was 3 ÷ 5 = 60%.
traits.why: A measured result is labeled as class test data, not an unsupported industry statistic.
